entries.note: This is a loopback-only desktop service. HTTP and WebSocket requests need the private runtime token and compatible Origin; it is not the Quest pairing protocol. Tokens stay in mode-0600 local state, never tracked files. Slow sockets reconnect to bounded retained output without stopping sessions. The retired browser bundle is not served; a later web client needs separate delivery authorization. State advertises handoff and desktopActions version 1. Presented requires a session attached on that socket. Desktop registration/action acknowledgement use the same authenticated events connection; discovery/reload route through the ephemeral desktop broker. These are local workflow bindings, not protection against an authenticated client deliberately forging readiness or displayed roots.

The host serves the format registry so a directly connected desktop and the service tests need no supervisor; the replaceable worker serves the same three routes for the live layered runtime whose host predates them. Both advertise formatRegistry: 1. Declared commands run only from format-preview (explicit open/refresh/agent call), never from tree listing. dashboard: 1 and projectGame: 1 tell connectors that the dashboard routes and that game-config/game answer from the per-project declaration; an older host still serves the game routes with the removed built-in semantics, which is why both tool families gate on their capability. game-config and game take an optional gameId selecting one declared game; omitted, both use the first declared record, which is what the launcher and an agent calling the tool without arguments get.
